newsitem.title: USA: Mass. attorney general files electric utility plan.
newsitem.headline: Mass. attorney general files electric utility plan.

text.p: Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger late Tuesday filed a final version of his plan to restructure the state's electric utility industry with the Department of Public Utilities.
Republican Gov. William Weld, who is running for the U.S. Senate against Democratic incumbent John Kerry, supports Harshbarger's plan, said Assistant Attorney General George Dean.
It also has the backing of a consortium of the state's largest industrial electricity customers, Dean said.

The final version, which is substantially the same as the one Harshbarger released two weeks ago, would allow Massachusetts residential and business consumers to choose their electric supplier on January 1, 1998. It would require all customers to be given an option that guarantees a minimum of 10 percent savings on their monthly bill.

In the meantime, New England Power Co, an affiliate of Massachusetts Electric, the state's largest retail electric company, announced it was selling its power plants in the towns of Somerset, Salem and Glouster.

David O'Connor, the Massachusetts Energy Resources Commissioner, said the move was a first in the country. "So far as I'm aware, no utility has voluntarily offered to fully divest its generation assets."
The sale means that New England Power will concentrate on distribution.

"These guys have a monopoly on the distribution, not the generation. They should take care of the knitting and just tend to the distribution by running the network, and leave generation to others," Dean said.
Dean said DPU approval is expected on or before December 1. A public hearing on the plan is scheduled for Wednesday.
